_comment: HAND batch assignments for AI functions no mechanical rule in gen_migration.py can classify.
propose_batch() deliberately emits 'unassigned' rather than guessing, and its batch_why says
'assign by hand before scheduling'. Until 2026-08-05 there was nowhere to record that hand
decision, so it was re-derived away on every regeneration -- which is why the AI ROOT itself sat
unscheduled for weeks while the ledger kept asking someone to schedule it.
Every entry MUST carry a `why`. The generator refuses the file otherwise. Keep the `why` about
the SCHEDULING decision (which batch, and what makes this function different); per-function RE
notes belong in the plate comment and docs/ai-closure.md.
TRIAGED TO ZERO 2026-08-06 (tracker item AI-BATCH-TRIAGE). The 25 that were still 'unassigned'
are assigned below. They were never blocked on anything -- they were invisible: AI1's done_when
reads 'every function IN THOSE BATCHES', so a function with no batch was in no item's acceptance
test and AI1 could have closed with 25 reachable AI functions untranslated. Assigning them by
sub-domain puts each one inside an existing gate rather than inventing a new one.
TWO FINDINGS ABOUT THE MECHANICAL RULES, recorded here rather than acted on -- BATCH_RULES is
deliberately left alone, for the reason AI1A already gives (a rule widened to catch one function
re-labels a finished batch):
1. The E rule keys on 'not reachable from players_tick', but the manifest's BFS is UNCUT (its
own _method_note) and walks through non-AI code, so a genuine event hook called ONLY from
outside the AI is 'reachable' and never gets E. That is exactly how llm_strat_ai_notify_
bldg_constructed -- three non-AI callers, no AI caller -- landed nowhere.
2. The substring rules produce false POSITIVES as well as gaps, and those look authoritative:
llm_strat_ai_notify_object_removed is batch C on 'move' matching inside 'reMOVEd'. It is not
re-labelled here (it is verified, and its batch is not what makes it correct) but a reader
comparing it against notify_bldg_constructed below deserves to know the C was an accident.
_section_A: A -- the pure island: target scan, engagement, candidate scratch.

why: llm_strat_ai_grid_match_stencil. Both callers (bldg_scan_grid_candidates, scan_build_site_
candidates) are batch A, and its sibling llm_strat_ai_grid_stencil_all_near_unthreatened is A
-- which matched only on the substring 'threat' inside 'unthreatened'. This one matches nothing.
AI1A's progress refuses to repair that by adding 'grid' to the batch-A key list, because the
same key would sweep in the influence-FLOOD family (grid_fill_below_threshold, grid_flood_step,
grid_stamp_seeds -- batch B below), i.e. re-open a finished batch to tidy a label. An override
is the mechanism that note did not yet have.
ALREADY `verified`: the pair was scheduled and rig-verified together. This records where the
work happened; AI1A's done_when ('every batch-A function verified') stays satisfied by it.
llm_strat_ai_unit_squad_firepower_value. Sole caller is llm_strat_ai_army_milestone_advance_
or_attack (batch A). It values a squad's firepower for the advance/attack decision -- engagement
scoring, not economy scoring, so B would be the wrong gate for it.
THIS ONE RE-OPENS AI1A (36/36 -> 36/37 verified). That is the intended effect and not a
regression: A's rig runs verified everything that was IN batch A, and this leaf never was. The
36 verified functions and their evidence are untouched.

_section_B: B -- economy, build queue, influence map (player_data readers only).

why: llm_strat_ai_update_opponent_relations. Called by player_tick; its own callees are batch B
(calc_mine_yield_estimate, score_build_categories) plus player_score_tier and unit_weapon_power
below. Writes player_data and nothing else, which is B's defining property.
llm_strat_ai_plan_construction. The construction planner: every callee but one is already batch
B (bldg_type_already_queued, plan_mine_construction, plan_turret_upgrade, react_resource_
shortage, rebalance_building_workers, queue_rotate_newest_to_front, maintain_unit_housing).
Unassigned only because 'construction' contains none of B's keys.
llm_strat_ai_recompute_shortage_state. Computes the resource-shortage state its already-batch-B
consumer react_resource_shortage acts on; shares player_score_tier with update_opponent_relations.
llm_strat_ai_grid_fill_below_threshold. Sole caller is llm_strat_ai_recompute_map_influence
(batch B); B's stated domain is 'economy, build queue, INFLUENCE MAP'. Note this is the
influence grid, NOT batch A's threat grid (grid_stamp_threat_ring / grid_clear_threat_bit).
llm_strat_ai_grid_flood_step. Same family and same sole caller as grid_fill_below_threshold --
the influence flood. Writes _G_LLM_STRAT_AI_GRID_WRAP_MASK, shared with the other two.
llm_strat_ai_grid_stamp_seeds. The influence flood's seeding step. Callers are notify_map_
changed / _2 (batch B below) and notify_object_removed (C by substring accident, see _comment).
Goes with the family it belongs to, not with either caller's label.
llm_strat_ai_calc_power_supply_ratio. Sole caller is plan_construction. POWER here is the
GENERATED RESOURCE (plants produce it, buildings consume it), not ENERGY the HP-like stat --
CLAUDE.md's domain note -- so this is an economy input and B is right.
llm_strat_ai_player_score_tier. Both callers are batch B (recompute_shortage_state,
update_opponent_relations). A scoring leaf with no callees.
llm_strat_ai_unit_weapon_power. Sole caller is update_opponent_relations. It is a SCORING leaf
-- weapon strength as an input to strategic assessment -- not combat execution, so it follows
its caller into B rather than into A.
llm_strat_ai_notify_map_changed. Re-stamps the influence grid through grid_stamp_seeds when the
map changes; called from bldg_queue_process_entry (B), plan_turret_upgrade (B), scan_
construction_sites (A) and notify_bldg_constructed (E below). Influence map = B.
llm_strat_ai_notify_map_changed_2. The near-identical sibling of the above (243 B vs 253 B, same
callee, two of the same callers). Scheduling them apart would be strictly worse: whichever is
translated second is a diff against the first.
llm_strat_ai_bldg_has_heli_unit. Sole caller is maintain_unit_housing (batch B) -- a housing/
capacity predicate over a building's occupants.
llm_strat_ai_bldg_count_by_category. Sole caller is score_build_categories (batch B); counts
owned buildings per category for the build-priority score.

_section_C: C -- group lifecycle + task machine + move execution.

why: llm_strat_ai_pick_owned_tile_or_home. Picks a destination tile for group movement; three of its
four callers are batch C (group_expansion_form_or_repurpose, group_reposition_members,
group_task_recall_home), the fourth is A's army_milestone_advance_or_attack.
llm_strat_ai_random_point_near. Movement math (cos/sin + the AI PRNG channel) behind the group
scatter workers; four of its five callers are batch C.
C's verified sites already REACH it -- layer 4 wired it as an ai_calls member bound to the
ORIGINAL after decompiling it. So this schedules the BODY; nothing in C is waiting on it.
llm_strat_ai_unit_is_order_pending. A 39-byte predicate; seven of its eight AI callers are batch
C group code (report_unit_states, reposition_members, the three scatter workers, nudge_
stragglers, tick_all_groups). The eighth is active_unit_tick, which goes to E below.
MOVED E -> D 2026-08-07 (user's call). THIS IS NOT ONLY THE AI'S DRIVER. It is the per-player
MOVE/TACTIC/STRATEGY scheduler, and the AI is one branch of it: it iterates EVERY claimed
player slot, advances ai_clock/_s/_t/_m for all of them unconditionally, and writes
width_m/height_m for everyone -- only the phase CALL is gated. The MOVE phase dispatches
llm_strat_ai_active_unit_tick when ai_enabled and llm_strat_unit_passive_engage_tick
OTHERWISE, so this function drives HUMAN players' passive engagement, and
llm_strat_unit_passive_engage_tick writes units[]. D is the roster-write burn-down and a
roster write is what this performs -- through a callee, which is exactly the class rule D
could not see before the roster_write_via column existed.
IT DOES NOT FOLLOW THAT AI2 CAN BURN IT DOWN. Routing this through orders would mean routing
the sim's own per-player scheduler through orders. The honest disposition is the subsystem
split (tracker AI-SPLIT), deferred behind SIM1. D membership RECORDS the coupling; it does not
schedule the fix, and AI2's narrowed scope explicitly excludes it.
CONSEQUENCE FOR AI1-P: player_data.ai_clock* is written for HUMAN players, so despite the name
it is NOT AI island data and must not travel with the island move.
The original batch-E rationale, still accurate about arming, follows.
THE AI ROOT (ai_migration.json `root`). Batch E is 'event hooks + boot/session-init,
caller-side entry', and the per-round phase driver is exactly that: it is entered from
llm_strat_sim_step once per sim step and hooks nothing below it that E does not already own.
TRANSLATE EARLY, VERIFY OFFLINE, NEVER ARM. Decided 2026-08-05.
Never arm: the three phase loops DELEGATE into effectively the whole AI closure, so a shadow
site here would have to declare the entire subtree's write set as extra_regions, and 'nested
sites do not compose' means arming it excludes every other AI site from the same rig run.
It is close to the worst shadow candidate in the cluster.
Verify offline instead: strip the outward calls and the body is pure scheduling over
player_data[].ai_clock{,_s,_t,_m} and three float periods (_G_LLM_STRAT_AI_STRATEGY_PERIOD
10.0 / _TACTIC_PERIOD 5.0 / _MOVE_PERIOD 1.0, the AI.SCR keywords fStrategyPeriod /
fTacticPeriod / fMovePeriod). That is the mh::orders::detail pattern from the reimpl-loop
skill -- take the state as a PARAMETER and cover it in `net_selftest aitest` over heap
buffers. Both interesting branches are trivially reachable offline and effectively
indistinguishable in the rig: a phase firing MULTIPLE times in one call when its period was
overshot by more than one interval, and ai_enabled routing the move phase to
llm_strat_ai_active_unit_tick vs llm_strat_unit_passive_engage_tick. That is a real T1, with
no game and no rig.
It stays the AI1-P promotion seam either way (Law 4: hook the closure's ROOTS only).
llm_strat_ai_notify_bldg_constructed. ALL THREE callers are outside the AI -- llm_bldg_construct
_finalize, llm_strat_bldg_state_construction, llm_strat_order_queue_dispatch. A build-completion
event hook that fires synchronously mid-sim, which is E's definition word for word.
It escaped the mechanical E rule because that rule asks 'not reachable from players_tick' and
the manifest's BFS is UNCUT: it walks non-AI code and reaches this through the sim. Finding 1
in _comment above.
llm_strat_ai_scr_parse. Callers are llm_strat_spawn_ai_base and llm_strat_spawn_invasion_force;
it reads AI.SCR out of the resource bank. Boot/session-init -- the other half of E's charter.
llm_strat_ai_player_tick. Sole caller is THE AI ROOT, and it is the per-player strategy/tactic
phase driver -- the same class of function as the root itself (0x004db905), which is why it goes
to the same batch.
TRANSLATE EARLY, VERIFY OFFLINE, NEVER ARM, for the root's stated reason: it delegates into most
of the closure, so a shadow site here would have to declare the whole subtree's write set, and
'nested sites do not compose' means arming it excludes every other AI site from that rig run.
llm_strat_ai_active_unit_tick. Sole caller is THE AI ROOT: it is the MOVE-phase driver the
root's own override names ('ai_enabled routing the move phase to llm_strat_ai_active_unit_tick
vs llm_strat_unit_passive_engage_tick').
THE NEVER-ARM CLAUSE THAT USED TO SIT HERE WAS WRONG, and it was wrong in the way this project
keeps being wrong: it said 'same never-arm argument as player_tick', which was copied from the
AI ROOT's stated reason rather than measured. tools/derive_write_closure.py, run 2026-08-07
before translating it: 48 reachable functions, ZERO escape candidates, an 11-region closure
(the four island regions + player_data directly; units, buildings, the three order regions and
_G_LLM_STRAT_RNG_STATE through its callees). player_tick's own numbers are 778 and 127 -- the
two are not the same shape at all, and only ONE of them delegates into most of the cluster.
It is SHADOW-ARMED as of AI1E slice 2 (tools/uiscripts/ini/shadow_ai_e1.ini), and its arm binds
live_calls() rather than shadow_calls(): a site that declares its whole closure must let every
outward call run FOR REAL, commit_attack_order included -- stubbing one whose writes the site
restores would guarantee the divergence it looks like it prevents.
The largest body in the cluster (1532 B) and review_required. It writes four batch-A island
regions (SCAN_TARGETS / ATTACK_CANDIDATES and their counts), so A's fixtures are the ones to
reuse when covering it offline -- the batch label is about WHERE IT IS ENTERED, not about which
data it touches.
llm_strat_ai_invasion_spawn_reinforcements. Its second caller, llm_strat_spawn_invasion_force,
is outside the AI -- a caller-side entry -- and it is the same outside caller scr_parse has, so
E keeps the whole invasion-spawn closure in one slice.
READ THE AI-READY ACK BEFORE TRANSLATING: it indexes with an UNINITIALISED min-tracker when no
element beats the seed. That is behaviour to reproduce, not a bug to fix.
llm_strat_ai_score_reinforcement_unit. Sole caller is invasion_spawn_reinforcements; a pure
scoring leaf that travels with its parent.
llm_strat_ai_create_reinforcement_unit. Sole caller is invasion_spawn_reinforcements.
FLAG FOR AI2: it reaches the sim roster through the engine's own creators (llm_strat_unit_create,
llm_unit_create_soldier) instead of writing units[] itself, which is exactly why rule D -- direct
roster writes -- does not catch it. When the R2 burn-down asks how the AI adds units, this is a
path batch D does not list.
